abstract: |
  Using daily means from the Rice Rivers Center buoy on the James River (January to March 2014), we asked whether river depth differed among months and between rainy and dry days. Depth rose through the winter, but only March differed from January, and rainy days were deeper than dry days, with no detectable month-by-weather interaction.
format: dyerlab-html
---

## Methods

**Data.** We used the water-quality record from the Rice Rivers Center buoy on the James River, stored as a CSV in the course data repository. The instruments take a reading every 15 minutes from January through March 2014. Readings 15 minutes apart are not independent of each other, so we averaged them into one value per day, and summed the rainfall for each day. Each day was assigned to its month, and classified as a *Rain* day if any rainfall was recorded and a *Dry* day otherwise.

```{r}
#| message: false
library( tidyverse )
library( lubridate )
library( knitr )
library( kableExtra )

url <- "https://dyerlabteaching.github.io/CourseData/Environmental/RiceRivers_2014.csv"

read_csv( url ) |>
  mutate( Date = as_date( mdy_hms( DateTime, tz = "EST" ) ) ) |>
  group_by( Date ) |>
  summarize( Rain = sum( Rain_in, na.rm = TRUE ),
             WaterTemp = mean( H2O_TempC, na.rm = TRUE ),
             DO = mean( ODO_mgl, na.rm = TRUE ),
             Depth = mean( Depth_m, na.rm = TRUE ) ) |>
  mutate( Month = droplevels( month( Date, label = TRUE ) ),
          Weather = factor( ifelse( Rain > 0, "Rain", "Dry" ) ) ) -> rice

summary( rice )
```

**Exploration.** The river is tidal, but its daily mean depth should track the volume of water coming downstream, which rain and seasonal runoff both increase. We plotted daily mean depth for each month, marking rainy and dry days.

```{r}
ggplot( rice, aes(x = Month, y = Depth) ) +
  geom_boxplot( outlier.shape = NA ) +
  geom_jitter( aes(color = Weather), width = 0.15 ) +
  ylab( "Daily Mean Depth (m)" )
```

**One-factor model.** We tested the null hypothesis that mean depth was the same in all three months ($H_O: \mu_{Jan} = \mu_{Feb} = \mu_{Mar}$) with a one-way analysis of variance, and calculated the fraction of the variation explained by month as $R^2 = SS_{Month} / SS_{Total}$.

```{r}
fit_month <- aov( Depth ~ Month, data = rice )
tab_month <- anova( fit_month )
tab_month
```

**Post hoc comparisons.** To find which months differed, we compared all pairs of months with Tukey's Honest Significant Differences.

```{r}
tuk_month <- TukeyHSD( fit_month )
tuk_month
plot( tuk_month )
```

**Two-factor model.** To ask whether rain changed depth, and whether its effect depended upon the month, we fit a two-factor model with month, weather, and their interaction, and summarized the mean depth and number of days in every month-by-weather combination (@tbl-depth).

```{r}
fit_both <- aov( Depth ~ Month * Weather, data = rice )
tab_both <- anova( fit_both )
tab_both
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-depth
#| tbl-cap: "Mean daily river depth (m) and number of days for each month and weather type at the Rice Rivers Center, January to March 2014."
rice |>
  group_by( Month, Weather ) |>
  summarize( Depth = mean( Depth ), Days = n() ) -> depth_means

depth_means |>
  kable( digits = 2 ) |>
  kable_paper( "striped", full_width = FALSE )
```

```{r}
ggplot( depth_means, aes(x = Month, y = Depth, color = Weather, group = Weather) ) +
  geom_point( size = 3 ) +
  geom_line() +
  ylab( "Mean Depth (m)" )
```

```{r}
N <- nrow( rice )
n_rain <- sum( rice$Weather == "Rain" )
F_month <- format( tab_month["Month", "F value"], digits = 3 )
df1_month <- tab_month["Month", "Df"]
df2_month <- tab_month["Residuals", "Df"]
P_month <- format( tab_month["Month", "Pr(>F)"], digits = 2 )
R2_month <- format( 100 * tab_month["Month", "Sum Sq"] / sum( tab_month$`Sum Sq` ), digits = 2 )
rise_JanMar <- format( 100 * tuk_month$Month["Mar-Jan", "diff"], digits = 2 )
P_JanMar <- format( tuk_month$Month["Mar-Jan", "p adj"], digits = 2 )
P_FebJan <- format( tuk_month$Month["Feb-Jan", "p adj"], digits = 2 )
P_MarFeb <- format( tuk_month$Month["Mar-Feb", "p adj"], digits = 2 )
F_weather <- format( tab_both["Weather", "F value"], digits = 3 )
df1_weather <- tab_both["Weather", "Df"]
df2_both <- tab_both["Residuals", "Df"]
P_weather <- format( tab_both["Weather", "Pr(>F)"], digits = 2 )
P_inter <- format( tab_both["Month:Weather", "Pr(>F)"], digits = 2 )
rain_minus_dry <- format( 100 * ( mean( rice$Depth[ rice$Weather == "Rain" ] ) -
                                  mean( rice$Depth[ rice$Weather == "Dry" ] ) ), digits = 2 )
```

## Results

Across the `r N` days of record, daily mean river depth differed among months (*F*~`r df1_month`,`r df2_month`~ = `r F_month`, *P* = `r P_month`), although month explained only `r R2_month`% of its variation. Depth rose through the winter, but the only pair of months that differed was March and January, with March averaging `r rise_JanMar` cm deeper (Tukey HSD, *P* = `r P_JanMar`); neither February and January (*P* = `r P_FebJan`) nor March and February (*P* = `r P_MarFeb`) differed. In the two-factor model, rainy days (`r n_rain` of `r N`) were deeper than dry days (*F*~`r df1_weather`,`r df2_both`~ = `r F_weather`, *P* = `r P_weather`), by `r rain_minus_dry` cm on average. The month-by-weather interaction was not significant (*P* = `r P_inter`): although rain appeared to raise the river most in March (@tbl-depth), there were only nine or ten rainy days per month, too few to show that the effect of rain differed among months.

## Questions

**Pairwise $t$-tests.** Three months make three pairs, so at $\alpha = 0.05$ the chance of at least one false positive when all three means are truly equal is $1 - (1 - 0.05)^3 \approx$ `r format( 1 - 0.95^3, digits = 2 )`, nearly three times the 5% we think we are testing at. The ANOVA tests the single hypothesis that all the means are equal at $\alpha$, and `TukeyHSD()` then builds its confidence intervals from the Studentized range, so the 95% level applies to the whole family of comparisons together rather than to each one separately.

**Daily means.** With all 8,199 readings the residual degrees of freedom would jump from `r df2_month` to about 8,196, the $F$ test would treat every reading as independent information, and even a tiny difference in depth would come out with a vanishingly small *P*-value. Readings 15 minutes apart are nearly copies of each other (pseudoreplication), so this violates the assumption that the observations are independent. Consecutive days are not fully independent either: a river that is high today is likely to be high tomorrow, so even the daily analysis somewhat overstates how much independent information we have, and the *P*-values should be read with that in mind.
